'''Shivaramakrishnan Pancharatnam''' (9 February 1934 – 28 May 1969) was an Indian physicist who did significant work in the field of optics. He is noted for his discovery of a type of [[geometric phase]] sometimes known as [[Geometric phase|Pancharatnam phase]] for polarized beams passing through crystals.<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Anandan |first1=Jeeva |last2=Christian |first2=Joy |year=1997 |title=Resource Letter GPP-1: Geometric Phases in Physics |journal=American Journal of Physics |volume=65 |issue=3 |pages=180–185 |doi= 10.1119/1.18570|arxiv = quant-ph/9702011 |bibcode = 1997AmJPh..65..180A |s2cid=119080820 }}</ref> 

==Biography==
He was born in [[Calcutta]] in [[West Bengal]], [[India]] in 1934.<ref name=series>{{cite journal |title=Foreword |journal=Current Science |date=1994 |volume=67 |issue=4 |pages=219 |jstor=24095725 }}</ref> His mother, {{ill|Sitalaxmi|qid=Q124416098|short=1}}, was [[C.V. Raman]]'s sister, and his father {{ill|Sivaramakrishnan (Indian Accounts Service)|lt=Sivaramakrishnan|qid=Q125516718|short=1}} worked in the Indian Accounts Service.<ref>{{cite Q|Q125516639}}</ref><ref>{{cite Q|Q125503928}}</ref>  He was elected a Fellow of the [[Indian Academy of Sciences]] at the early age of 25. He was a reader at the Department of studies in Physics, [[University of Mysore]] from 1961–1964.<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://uomphysics.net/faculty/former-fac.php |title=Former Faculty |access-date=23 April 2015 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150225003137/http://uomphysics.net/faculty/former-fac.php |archive-date=25 February 2015 |url-status=dead |df=dmy-all }}</ref> From 1964 until his death in 1969 at the age of 35 he was a Research Fellow of [[St Catherine's College, Oxford]], working in association with [[George William Series]]. His publications for this period were mainly concerned with the theory of effects found in experiments on [[optical pumping]], e.g. double refraction in a gas due to spin alignment. Professor Series has written an introduction to the life and work of Pancharatnam. He also prepared, for the [[Proceedings of the Royal Society]], the last three papers from notes left by Pancharatnam.<ref>{{Cite journal |doi = 10.1088/0031-8949/1997/T70/E02|title = George W Series Memorial Essays |journal = Physica Scripta|volume=1997 |issue=T70 |pages = 5|year = 1997|last1 = Dodd|first1 = J. N.|doi-access = free}}</ref>

In 1956, Pancharatnam was studying [[Interference (wave propagation)|interference]] figures produced by light waves in [[crystal]] plates, under his advisor [[C. V. Raman]], when he discovered the properties of what is now known as the [[geometric phase]], and which predated [[Michael Berry (physicist)|Michael Berry]]'s work on the topic from 1983.<ref name=berry>{{cite journal |last1=Berry |first1=Michael |title=Pancharatnam, virtuoso of the Poincaré sphere: an appreciation |journal=Current Science |date=1994 |volume=67 |issue=4 |pages=220–223 |jstor=24095727 }}</ref>
